meta.title: Final historical ranking for montage
meta.wealth_note: wealth is now a simplified on-screen value without date or peak-year qualifiers.
meta.country_note: Country reflects the primary public country association used for the final montage dataset.
meta.wealth_source_note: wealth_source is a short plain-English business label for broad audiences.
meta.source_detail_note: source_detail is now written in more natural spoken English, with less corporate phrasing and less repetition.
meta.wealth_origin_note: wealth_origin shows whether the fortune was self-made, inherited, inherited and expanded, widow inheritance, family business, family wealth or divorce settlement.
meta.money_from_note: Use money_from for on-screen cards: it names the business in simple global English first, then the brand in brackets when helpful.
meta.name_note: name is now simplified for display and does not include trailing family markers.

entries.name: Hetty Green
entries.source_detail: She made her money the old Wall Street way, snapping up distressed bonds, making loans and buying property.
entries.fact: Nicknamed the 'Witch of Wall Street', she became one of the most notorious financiers of the Gilded Age.
entries.money_from: Cheap bonds, loans and real estate

entries.name: Madam C. J. Walker
entries.source_detail: Her fortune grew out of haircare and beauty products created for Black women.
entries.fact: She is widely remembered as America's first female self-made millionaire and built her wealth through Black haircare products.

entries.name: Annie Turnbo Malone
entries.source_detail: Before Walker, Malone was already making serious money from Poro hair products and beauty training.
entries.fact: Before Madam C. J. Walker became famous, Malone had already created one of the largest Black-owned beauty businesses in America.

entries.name: Marjorie Merriweather Post
entries.source_detail: The family cereal money was the starting point; she then helped turn it into the much larger General Foods empire.
entries.fact: She turned the Post cereal inheritance into a global food empire and later owned Mar-a-Lago.
entries.money_from: Cereal and packaged food (Post / General Foods)

entries.name: Brooke Astor
entries.source_detail: This was old Astor money, rooted in prime New York real estate.
entries.fact: Her name became synonymous with old New York wealth, society philanthropy and a major elder-abuse court case after her decline.
entries.money_from: New York real estate inheritance (Astor family)

entries.name: Huguette Clark
entries.source_detail: Her wealth was inherited from her father, who made a fortune in copper.
entries.fact: She became a legend for living reclusively while leaving behind mansions, paintings and a fortune that fueled years of legal battles.

entries.name: Barbara Hutton
entries.source_detail: She was born into the Woolworth store fortune.
entries.fact: Known as the 'poor little rich girl', she inherited the Woolworth fortune as one of the world's most famous heiresses.

entries.name: Doris Duke
entries.source_detail: The Duke billions came from tobacco, electricity and a long list of investments.
entries.fact: She mixed tobacco money with lavish patronage of art, gardens and architecture on several continents.

entries.name: Dirce Navarro De Camargo
entries.source_detail: Her family's wealth was built in Brazil through construction, cement and energy.
entries.fact: Around 2012-2013 she was widely described as the richest woman in Brazil, which gives the video a strong Latin American business chapter outside the usual U.S.-Europe focus.

entries.name: Doris Fisher
entries.source_detail: Gap was the source of her fortune; she built it from one clothing store into a huge chain.
entries.fact: She helped turn Gap from a single store into one of the biggest clothing chains in America.

entries.name: Helen Walton
entries.source_detail: Her money came from Walmart, the low-price retail giant built by the Walton family.
entries.fact: She helped build Walmart in its early years before becoming one of the richest women in the world.

entries.name: Anne Cox Chambers
entries.source_detail: She inherited Cox wealth from newspapers, TV stations and cable systems.
entries.fact: She co-owned the family company Cox Enterprises, a privately held media empire, with her sister Barbara Cox Anthony for 33 years.

entries.name: Leona Helmsley
entries.source_detail: Hotels and Manhattan real estate made her rich.
entries.fact: After allegations of non-payment were made by contractors hired to improve Helmsley's Connecticut home, she was investigated and convicted of federal income tax evasion and other crimes in 1989.
entries.money_from: Luxury hotels and New York real estate

entries.name: Barbara Cox Anthony
entries.source_detail: She inherited Cox wealth from newspapers, TV stations and cable systems.
entries.fact: She and her sister controlled one of America's largest private media companies, Cox Enterprises.

entries.name: Liliane Bettencourt
entries.source_detail: Most of her money came from L'Oreal, the beauty empire behind makeup, skincare and hair products.
entries.fact: She was a board member and one of the principal shareholders of L'Oréal.

entries.name: Marguerite Harbert
entries.source_detail: The Harbert fortune started in construction and later spread into investments.
entries.fact: She became one of the richest women in America through the Harbert family construction and investment fortune.

entries.name: Birgit Rausing
entries.source_detail: Think drink cartons: the family fortune came from Tetra Pak packaging.
entries.fact: The Rausing family became globally known because Tetra Pak changed how milk and juice were packaged and sold.
entries.money_from: Drink cartons and food packaging (Tetra Pak)

entries.name: Johanna Quandt
entries.source_detail: Her fortune was tied to the family's big stake in BMW.
entries.fact: When she died in 2015 she was the 8th richest person in Germany (and the richest German woman), the 77th richest person in the world, and the 11th richest woman worldwide according to Forbes.

entries.name: Joan Kroc
entries.source_detail: She inherited McDonald's money after Ray Kroc died.
entries.fact: She gave away billions to charity and left huge gifts to the Salvation Army and public broadcasting.

entries.name: Kwong Siu-hing
entries.source_detail: Her wealth came from Hong Kong property, especially the giant developer Sun Hung Kai.
entries.fact: She controls the conglomerate Sun Hung Kai Properties, the largest property developer in Hong Kong as of 2019.
entries.money_from: Apartment buildings and property (Sun Hung Kai)

entries.name: Susan Thompson Buffett
entries.source_detail: The fortune was tied to Berkshire Hathaway, Warren Buffett's investing empire.
entries.fact: It was known simply as the Buffett Foundation until 2004, when it was renamed in honor of Susan Buffett, who died that year.

entries.name: Lily Safra
entries.source_detail: This was banking money, from the Safra family's private-bank fortune.
entries.fact: She had a significant art collection and owned the historic Villa Leopolda on the French Riviera.

entries.name: Eva Gonda de Rivera
entries.source_detail: The family got rich from convenience stores and soft drinks through FEMSA, OXXO and Coca-Cola bottling.
entries.fact: Along with her daughters, she owns a major stake in the FEMSA beverage corporation, which operates convenience stores and bottling plants across Mexico and Latin America.
entries.money_from: Convenience stores and soft drinks (OXXO / Coca-Cola bottling)

entries.name: Nina Wang
entries.source_detail: Her fortune came through Chinachem, a Hong Kong business built around property and chemicals.
entries.fact: She was the widow of Hong Kong chemical magnate Teddy Wang, who was kidnapped and disappeared in 1990.

entries.name: Barbara Piasecka Johnson
entries.source_detail: She became enormously rich through the Johnson & Johnson family fortune.
entries.fact: She rose from being a household employee to one of the world's most talked-about heiresses after marrying into the Johnson family.

entries.name: Judy Love
entries.source_detail: Her money came from Love's, the highway chain of gas stations, truck stops and roadside stores.
entries.fact: She and Tom Love launched the business in 1964 with a $5,000 loan, making her one of the clearest examples of a large modern fortune built from highway retail rather than inheritance.
entries.money_from: Highway gas stations and truck stops (Love's)

entries.name: Maria Franca Fissolo
entries.source_detail: This is Ferrero money, from Nutella and other global sweets brands.
entries.fact: Before marrying Michele Ferrero, she reportedly worked as his secretary, and she remained part of one of Europe's most famous confectionery dynasties for decades.

entries.name: Jacqueline Mars
entries.source_detail: She inherited Mars money, from candy, snacks and pet food.
entries.fact: She is the daughter of Audrey Ruth (Meyer) and Forrest Mars Sr., and the granddaughter of Franklin Clarence Mars, founders of the American candy company Mars Inc.

entries.name: Marilyn Carlson Nelson
entries.source_detail: The fortune came from hotels and travel services through the Carlson group.
entries.fact: She shares ownership of the company with her sister, Barbara Carlson Gage.

entries.name: Elaine Wynn
entries.source_detail: Las Vegas casinos and luxury hotels were the source of her wealth.
entries.fact: She helped shape modern Las Vegas through casinos, resorts and high-profile divorce battles.

entries.name: Barbara Carlson Gage
entries.source_detail: The fortune came from hotels and travel services through the Carlson group.
entries.fact: She is part of the same family business dynasty as Marilyn Carlson Nelson, which makes the Carlson sisters an important travel-industry chapter in the historical timeline.

entries.name: Friede Springer
entries.source_detail: Her money came from Axel Springer, a giant media company built on newspapers, magazines and digital news.
entries.fact: She is the main owner of the Axel Springer SE media conglomerate - and thus of Europe's largest newspaper Bild - being one of the richest people of Germany.
entries.money_from: Newspapers, magazines and digital media (Axel Springer)

entries.name: Iris Fontbona
entries.source_detail: Mining is at the heart of this fortune, especially copper.
entries.fact: After her husband's death, she became the face of one of Latin America's biggest mining and business empires.

entries.name: Massimiliana Landini Aleotti
entries.source_detail: Her wealth comes from Menarini, a major medicines business.
entries.fact: She is the co-owner of the pharmaceutical company Menarini based in Florence, Tuscany, and one of the world's ten richest women.

entries.name: Antonia Ax:son Johnson
entries.source_detail: This family fortune was built in trade, energy and industry.
entries.fact: In 1982 she succeeded her father as chairman of the board for Axel Johnson AB, Sweden, and Axel Johnson Inc., Stamford, US According to Forbes Johnson was the third richest Swedish billionaire in 2013.

entries.name: Charlotte Colket Weber
entries.source_detail: She inherited Campbell Soup money.
entries.fact: Her fortune comes from the Dorrance family, the dynasty behind Campbell Soup.
entries.money_from: Canned soup and packaged food (Campbell Soup)

entries.name: Rosalia Mera
entries.source_detail: She co-built the business that became Zara and the Inditex fashion empire.
entries.fact: At the time of her death, she was the richest woman in Spain and the world's richest self-made woman according to Forbes.
entries.money_from: Clothing stores and fast fashion (Zara / Inditex)

entries.name: Elaine Marshall
entries.source_detail: Her fortune comes from Koch Industries, a private giant in oil, chemicals, fertilizer and pipelines.
entries.fact: After her husband's death, she became one of the biggest female fortunes connected to Koch Industries.
entries.money_from: Oil, chemicals, fertilizer and pipelines (Koch Industries)

entries.name: Miriam Adelson
entries.source_detail: Casino resorts made this fortune.
entries.fact: She became one of the world's richest women after inheriting Sheldon Adelson's casino empire.

entries.name: Rafaela Aponte-Diamant
entries.source_detail: She built her wealth in cargo shipping, moving containers around the world by sea.
entries.fact: She is one of the few self-made women at the very top of global wealth rankings, thanks to shipping rather than tech or fashion.

entries.name: Diane Hendricks
entries.source_detail: She made her fortune selling roofing, siding and other construction supplies.
entries.fact: She is the widow of the late businessman Ken Hendricks.
entries.money_from: Roofing, siding and building supplies (ABC Supply)

entries.name: Sherry Brydson
entries.source_detail: This is old media money, tied to Thomson Reuters and related holdings.
entries.fact: Her fortune shows that some of the world's biggest female fortunes still come from old media dynasties, not consumer brands.
entries.money_from: News, financial data and media holdings

entries.name: Ann Walton Kroenke
entries.source_detail: She inherited part of the Walmart fortune.
entries.fact: Heiress to the Walmart fortune, Ann and her sister, Nancy Walton Laurie, inherited stock from their father, Bud Walton, who was the brother and an early business partner of Walmart founder Sam Walton.

entries.name: Alice Walton
entries.source_detail: She inherited part of the Walmart fortune.
entries.fact: As of July 2025, Walton has an estimated net worth of $116 billion, making her the richest woman in the world and 15th richest person overall, according to the Bloomberg Billionaires Index.

entries.name: Christy Walton
entries.source_detail: Her wealth came from the Walmart fortune after her husband's death.
entries.fact: Her wealth jumped after the death of John Walton, making her one of the best-known Walmart heirs.

entries.name: Miuccia Prada
entries.source_detail: She turned Prada into a global luxury-fashion powerhouse.
entries.fact: She is the head designer of Prada and the founder of its subsidiary Miu Miu.
entries.money_from: Luxury clothes, bags and fashion brands (Prada)

entries.name: Christina Onassis
entries.source_detail: The money came from the Onassis shipping fortune.
entries.fact: After the death of Aristotle Onassis, she became the public face of one of the world's most famous shipping fortunes.

entries.name: Mary Alice Dorrance Malone
entries.source_detail: She inherited Campbell Soup money.
entries.fact: She appears in Forbes' 2002 historical women ranking, which helps anchor the pre-2000 part of the video.
entries.money_from: Canned soup and packaged food (Campbell Soup)

entries.name: Blair Parry-Okeden
entries.source_detail: Her fortune came from Cox, a media and cable empire.
entries.fact: According to Forbes Asia, she was Australia's richest person by net worth in 2016.

entries.name: Esther Koplowitz
entries.source_detail: She became rich through FCC, a business built on construction, water systems and city services.
entries.fact: She became one of Spain's richest women through FCC, a giant company in construction, water and city services.

entries.name: Savitri Jindal
entries.source_detail: The family money came from steel, power and big infrastructure projects.
entries.fact: After her husband's death, she became the public face of one of India's biggest industrial families.

entries.name: Beate Heister
entries.source_detail: She inherited Aldi supermarket money.
entries.fact: She is one of the two children of Karl Albrecht, who founded the discount supermarket chain Aldi with his brother Theo.

entries.name: Carrie Perrodo
entries.source_detail: Her wealth comes from Perenco, an oil and gas business.
entries.fact: She is the owner of the oil group Perenco, which was founded by her late husband Hubert.

entries.name: Marilyn Simons
entries.source_detail: This fortune was made in hedge funds, through Renaissance Technologies.
entries.fact: Her fortune links Wall Street money with major philanthropy in mathematics, autism research and basic science rather than with a consumer brand most viewers would instantly recognize.

entries.name: Nancy Walton Laurie
entries.source_detail: She inherited part of the Walmart fortune.
entries.fact: She is one of several Walton heirs whose fortunes came from the rise of Walmart.

entries.name: Kirsten Rausing
entries.source_detail: Packaging made this fortune, especially the drink-carton business behind Tetra Laval.
entries.fact: She was listed as the 150th richest individual in the world in the Forbes 2020 list of The World's Billionaires.

entries.name: Vicky Safra
entries.source_detail: The money came from the Safra banking empire.
entries.fact: The Safra family became globally known through private banking and large cross-border financial deals.

entries.name: Francoise Bettencourt Meyers
entries.source_detail: Most of her wealth comes from L'Oreal.
entries.fact: She became the public face of the L'Oreal fortune as the family's wealth reached record levels.

entries.name: Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw
entries.source_detail: She built her fortune in biotech, especially medicines like insulin.
entries.fact: She is the executive chairperson and founder of Biocon Limited and Biocon Biologics Limited, a biotechnology company based in Bangalore, India and the former chairperson of Indian Institute of Management, Bangalore.

entries.name: Alicia Koplowitz
entries.source_detail: She started with construction money and turned a lot of it into investments.
entries.fact: When her father died, she and her sister inherited Fomento de Construcciones y Contratas, S.A.

entries.name: Charlene de Carvalho-Heineken
entries.source_detail: Her wealth comes from Heineken beer.
entries.fact: As of July 2024, Forbes estimated her net worth at US$14.1 billion.

entries.name: Gina Rinehart
entries.source_detail: Mining made her rich, especially iron ore.
entries.fact: She is the executive chairman of Hancock Prospecting, a privately owned mineral exploration and extraction company founded by her father, Lang Hancock.

entries.name: Oprah Winfrey
entries.source_detail: Her money came from television, production deals and owning media businesses.
entries.fact: She became one of the few women on the list whose fortune came mainly from media power rather than inheritance.
entries.money_from: TV shows, media company and production deals

entries.name: Ronda Stryker
entries.source_detail: She inherited the fortune behind Stryker's hospital beds, surgical tools and medical equipment.
entries.fact: Her fortune traces back to the medical beds and surgical devices invented by her grandfather Homer Stryker.
entries.money_from: Hospital beds, surgical tools and medical devices (Stryker)

entries.name: Trudy Cathy White
entries.source_detail: The family money comes from Chick-fil-A restaurants.
entries.fact: The Cathy family fortune is unusual because it comes from a private fast-food chain that still closes on Sundays.

entries.name: Shari Arison
entries.source_detail: Her wealth traces back to cruise ships and banking.
entries.fact: She is the owner of Arison Investments, which consists of several companies, and of The Ted Arison Family Foundation, which comprises several philanthropic organizations that operate as its subsidiaries.

entries.name: Zhang Yin
entries.source_detail: She made her money turning recycled paper into cardboard and packaging.
entries.fact: She became famous for building a paper empire from recycled cardboard and shipping boxes.
entries.money_from: Cardboard boxes and packaging paper (Nine Dragons Paper)

entries.name: Valerie Mars
entries.source_detail: She inherited Mars money, from candy, snacks and pet food.
entries.fact: As of June 2021, Bloomberg Billionaires Index estimated her wealth to be $11.5 billion.

entries.name: Abigail Johnson
entries.source_detail: Her fortune comes from Fidelity, which manages savings, retirement money and investment funds.
entries.fact: She turned a family-controlled financial company into an even bigger investing giant in the digital era.
entries.money_from: Savings, retirement accounts and investment funds (Fidelity)

entries.name: Zhong Huijuan
entries.source_detail: She built her wealth in prescription medicines.
entries.fact: She is the founder, CEO, and chair of Hansoh Pharmaceutical, which is headquartered in Lianyungang and is traded on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange.

entries.name: Margarita Louis-Dreyfus
entries.source_detail: This is commodity-trading money: grain, cotton and other raw materials.
entries.fact: She stepped into a centuries-old trading empire that moves grain, cotton and other commodities around the world.
entries.money_from: Buying and selling grain, cotton and other raw materials

entries.name: Susanne Klatten
entries.source_detail: Her wealth comes from BMW on one side and chemicals on the other.
entries.fact: As of January 2022, her net worth was estimated at US$23.4 billion, making her the wealthiest woman in Germany and the 50th richest person in the world according to the Bloomberg Billionaires Index.

entries.name: Laurene Powell Jobs
entries.source_detail: A lot of her money comes from Apple and Disney shares, plus investments of her own.
entries.fact: Unlike many tech heirs, she built a high-profile second act as an investor, media owner and philanthropist.

entries.name: Maria Asuncion Aramburuzabala
entries.source_detail: The fortune started with Corona beer money and grew further through investments.
entries.fact: She is the chairperson of Tresalia Capital, a venture capital firm.
entries.money_from: Beer and investment deals (Corona / Grupo Modelo)

entries.name: Yelena Baturina
entries.source_detail: She made her money in real estate and construction materials.
entries.fact: For a long stretch she was the most famous female billionaire in Russia, which makes her an important bridge between the 1990s and the present day.
entries.money_from: Real estate development and building materials

entries.name: Melinda French Gates
entries.source_detail: Most of her wealth came from Microsoft-related assets and later investments.
entries.fact: She turned a tech-fortune profile into an independent identity in philanthropy, health and investing.

entries.name: Wu Yajun
entries.source_detail: She got rich building homes and residential property in China.
entries.fact: She is the co-founder, chairwoman, and former CEO of Longfor Properties.

entries.name: J. K. Rowling
entries.source_detail: Harry Potter is where the money came from: books, films, royalties and related products.
entries.fact: She is best known for writing Harry Potter, a seven-volume series about a young wizard.
entries.money_from: Harry Potter books, films and royalties

entries.name: Marijke Mars
entries.source_detail: She inherited Mars money, from candy, snacks and pet food.
entries.fact: She is one of the Mars heirs, a family that stayed wealthy by keeping its candy empire private.

entries.name: Denise Coates
entries.source_detail: She built her fortune in online betting and casino games.
entries.fact: She is the founder, majority shareholder and joint chief executive of online gambling company, bet365.
entries.money_from: Online sports betting and casino games (bet365)

entries.name: Renata Kellnerova
entries.source_detail: The family money came from lending, telecom and investments through PPF.
entries.fact: She became one of Europe's richest women after inheriting the PPF fortune founded by Petr Kellner.

entries.name: Wang Laichun
entries.source_detail: She made her money supplying cables, connectors and other parts for phones and electronics.
entries.fact: Founded in 2004 in Dongguan, China, the company designs and manufacturers computer cables; it is also a key assembler of AirPods for Apple.
entries.money_from: Phone cables, connectors and electronics parts (Luxshare)

entries.name: Sandra Ortega Mera
entries.source_detail: She inherited a big stake in Zara's parent company.
entries.fact: Mera is the daughter of Amancio Ortega Gaona, and his first wife Rosalia Mera, the founders of Inditex, best known as the parent company of global fashion empire Zara.
entries.money_from: Clothing stores and fashion retail shares (Zara / Inditex)

entries.name: MacKenzie Scott
entries.source_detail: Most of her money came from Amazon shares she received after her divorce from Jeff Bezos.
entries.fact: She was married to Jeff Bezos, the co-founder of Amazon, from 1993 to 2019.

entries.name: Zhou Qunfei
entries.source_detail: She got rich making smartphone screens and touch glass.
entries.fact: After the public listing of her company on the Shenzhen ChiNext market in March 2015, her net worth reached US$10 billion, making her the richest woman in China.
entries.money_from: Smartphone screens and touch glass (Lens Technology)

entries.name: Sara Blakely
entries.source_detail: She built her fortune selling Spanx shapewear.
entries.fact: She founded Spanx, an intimate apparel company with pants and leggings, in Atlanta, Georgia.

entries.name: Lyndal Stephens Greth
entries.source_detail: This is oil money, built in the energy business.
entries.fact: Her sudden rise shows how a single giant oil fortune can create a new billionaire almost overnight.

entries.name: Tatyana Kim
entries.source_detail: She made her money by turning Wildberries into a giant online store for clothes, shoes and everyday goods.
entries.fact: She started with small online sales from home and turned the business into a national shopping giant.

entries.name: Julia Koch
entries.source_detail: Her fortune comes from Koch Industries, which makes money from oil, chemicals, fertilizer, pipelines and trading.
entries.fact: After David Koch's death, she became one of the wealthiest women in America almost instantly.
entries.money_from: Oil, chemicals, fertilizer, pipelines and trading (Koch)

entries.name: Yang Huiyan
entries.source_detail: She became rich through one of China's biggest homebuilding companies.
entries.fact: She is the chairwoman and the majority shareholder of Country Garden Holdings, a stake largely transferred to her by her father Yang Guoqiang in 2007.

entries.name: Athina Onassis
entries.source_detail: What remained of the family wealth came from the Onassis shipping fortune.
entries.fact: She inherited the last direct line of the Onassis fortune and became a media phenomenon from childhood.

entries.name: Rihanna
entries.source_detail: Most of her money came from beauty and lingerie businesses, not from music.
entries.fact: Her billionaire story is unusual because the biggest driver was Fenty Beauty rather than concert income alone.

entries.name: Taylor Swift
entries.source_detail: Her fortune was built on songs, streaming and enormous concert tours.
entries.fact: She became the rare billionaire whose fortune was attributed mainly to songs, touring and ownership around her music career.
